questions.question: When operating a school bus, when should mirrors be adjusted?
questions.explanation: Mirrors must be properly adjusted for safe school bus operation. Always check and adjust each mirror before you drive.

questions.question: What is brake lag?

options.text: The delay between pressing the brake pedal and the brakes starting to work.
The distance between the brake pedal and the floor.
The amount of air pressure used to stop the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: The delay between pressing the brake pedal and the brakes starting to work.
questions.explanation: Air brakes cannot work instantly because air takes time to travel through the brake lines. There is usually at least a half-second delay between pressing the brake pedal and the brakes starting to work.

questions.question: Passengers may not stand in front of the:
questions.explanation: On buses that allow standing passengers, no one may stand in front of the rear of the driver's seat. A line on the floor marks this area. This line is called the standee line.

questions.question: During the vehicle inspection test, you must be able to do all of the following, except:

options.text: Point out where the dipstick is located.
Show that the engine oil is at a safe level.
Show that the oil is below the refill mark.

questions.correctAnswerText: Show that the oil is below the refill mark.
questions.explanation: During the pre-trip vehicle inspection, you will show where the dipstick is and prove the oil level is safe and above the refill mark.

questions.question: For a single vehicle with air brakes, the leakage rate during a static test should be no more than ____ in one minute.
questions.explanation: During a static leakage test, air should leak from the system at no more than 2 psi per minute. If it leaks faster, the vehicle needs repairs and should not be driven.

questions.question: Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS):

options.text: Work with other brake systems and do not reduce braking power.
Are not effective on larger vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Work with other brake systems and do not reduce braking power.
questions.explanation: ABS works alongside the regular braking system. It does not increase or decrease overall braking power. ABS only activates when the wheels are about to lock.

questions.question: What do air brakes use to make the brakes work?
questions.explanation: Many large vehicles use air brakes. These systems use compressed air to operate.

questions.question: Except for straight line backing, how many times may you exit your vehicle to check its position during testing?
questions.explanation: You may exit your vehicle to check its position during any test exercise. This is called a look. During straight line backing, you may only look once. During all other exercises, you may look up to two times.

questions.question: A safety valve opens at ____ pounds per square inch (psi).
questions.explanation: The safety valve protects air tanks and the brake system from too much air pressure. It usually opens at 150 psi.

questions.question: When approaching a drawbridge with a green light:

options.text: You must wait for the light to change to yellow.

questions.explanation: A bus does not need to stop before crossing a drawbridge with a green signal light. However, you should still slow down and make sure it is safe before crossing.

questions.question: Air tank drains should:

options.text: Not be used by the driver.
Only be used when it is wet outside.
Be used to drain the tanks completely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be used to drain the tanks completely.
questions.explanation: Compressed air in air brake systems contains water and oil. These liquids damage brakes if they build up. Drivers must open air tank drains daily to remove this buildup.

questions.question: When driving with passengers, a bus driver should:

options.text: Engage in conversation with the passengers.
Not engage in conversation with passengers.
Ask passengers to watch out the windows for hazards.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not engage in conversation with passengers.
questions.explanation: Bus drivers must not talk with passengers. Conversation distracts the driver from focusing on the road.

questions.question: Truck tractors with air brakes built on or after March 1, 1997 must have:
questions.explanation: All truck tractors with air brakes built on or after March 1, 1997 must have anti-lock brakes.

questions.question: Fueling a bus while passengers are on board is:

options.text: Recommended, but only if the passengers are told about the refueling.
Recommended, but only if time is an issue.

questions.explanation: Do not refuel a bus while passengers are on board unless absolutely necessary. Never refuel a bus with passengers inside an enclosed building.

questions.question: Brake linings should be:
questions.explanation: Brake linings must not be loose or soaked with oil or grease. They must not be dangerously thin.

questions.question: ABS allows a driver to:

options.text: Maintain control of their vehicle while braking.
See farther ahead of their vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Maintain control of their vehicle while braking.
questions.explanation: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) prevents wheel lockup. It helps drivers keep control of their vehicle when braking on slippery surfaces.

questions.question: Carry-on baggage:

options.text: May be left in the aisle.
Must be secured away from exits.
Should be placed near the doors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must be secured away from exits.
questions.explanation: Baggage must not be left in doorways or aisles. All baggage must be secured so it does not block exits, prevents the driver from moving freely, or injures passengers if it shifts.

questions.question: Before a trip, you should make sure that:

options.text: The grooved pedal surface has not been smoothed out.

questions.correctAnswerText: The grooved pedal surface has not been smoothed out.
questions.explanation: Before your trip, check that pedals work properly and nothing blocks them. Make sure grooved pedal surfaces are not worn smooth.

questions.question: During the basic control skills test, you will receive points if you:
questions.explanation: The examiner counts each time your vehicle touches or crosses a boundary line. Each error lowers your skills test score.

questions.question: When inspecting the interior of a bus, you should:
questions.explanation: When inspecting a bus interior, make sure all handholds and railings are secure and safe for passengers to use.
